questions.q: Why keep three screenshots, not just the latest one?
questions.a: The docs don't say why. A likely reason: to check that an action worked, the agent compares the screen before and after it, and one screenshot can't show a change.

teach.title: How it works: memory in parts

questions.q: What goes in the progress log?
questions.a: The goal, the list of steps with done or not done, the last state the agent confirmed, and any values it has typed, such as ids or totals.

questions.q: How would you show the fix worked?
questions.a: Rerun the 300-step job and count repeated actions: the same action on the same item twice. Compare that count, and the success rate, before and after.

questions.q: Why won't a 2-million-token window fix the repeats?
questions.a: Room isn't the problem. The agent has to find which steps are done among many look-alike screenshots, models get worse at that as the context grows, and a bigger window only adds more of them.
As the context grows, the model gets worse at recalling and using what's in it, especially when similar-looking distractors are present.

questions.q: Name three parts of a better memory for this agent.
questions.a: A written progress log it updates every step, only the last few screenshots in context, and a check after each action that it worked.
